title: Cyrus and the Compass
premise: When bush pilot Noor Ashgrove salvages a sealed chest from a flooded river bend, she finds documents proving a massacred border village was destroyed on official orders—and that the man who signed them now governs the territory she flies. Pursued by a 'salvage inspector' who is really an assassin, Noor teams up with Cyrus Vane, a disgraced archivist who has spent ten years chasing the same truth, and the two run the monsoon-swollen rivers toward the capital's last honest court. Betrayed by the ally sheltering them and nearly drowned in the flood that takes her plane, Noor must choose between destroying the evidence to save Cyrus or delivering it and losing everything she built in the interior. She delivers it: the governor falls, Cyrus's name is restored, and Noor—changed by what memory demands—keeps flying, but no longer to stay invisible.
about_author: Sebastian Ravensworth is the pen name of a former river surveyor who spent six years mapping waterways that appear on no tourist map. He writes adventure novels where the landscape is the most honest character and the past refuses to stay submerged.

chapters.title: The River Keeps What It Is Given
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Flying a medicine run through storm weather, she spots a glinting chest snagged in a flooded river bend and winches it aboard against her better judgment. The beat is wary curiosity—the wilderness has taught her that gifts from the water are rarely free.

chapters.title: A Dead Nation's Seal
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, night at her airstrip shack. Prying the chest open, she finds archival documents stamped with the seal of Kestria, a nation officially erased from maps twenty years ago. The beat is dread dawning into resolve: the papers name orders, signatures, a village called Merrow's Bend.

chapters.title: The Man Who Reads Water
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Introduced hiding in a fishing camp downstream, Cyrus Vane recognizes Noor's plane by its engine sound and intercepts her at the fuel dock, begging to see what she pulled from the river. The beat is two guarded strangers recognizing the same hunger.

chapters.title: Merrow's Bend, 1994
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The documents reveal the village was razed on orders signed by Governor Aldous Crane—Cyrus's former mentor. Cyrus confesses his disgrace: he falsified an archive entry to bury this once, and has regretted it for a decade. The beat is shame meeting a second chance.

chapters.title: The Salvage Inspector
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A courteous government man, Inspector Hale, arrives asking about 'recovered property of historical value,' his questions a little too precise. Noor lies fluently and hates how easily it comes. The beat is the moment invisibility stops being a shield.

chapters.title: Fuel, Lies, and Leaking Seams
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. They prepare Noor's aging river boat for the run to the capital, patching seams and hiding documents in the ballast. Cyrus notices Noor's hands shake when she talks about the village she once flew medicine to and never landed at. The beat is tenderness under pressure.

chapters.title: Departure Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. They slip downstream ahead of the monsoon's first wall of rain, Hale's boat visible behind them at the bend. Noor torches a decoy copy in the shack to buy time. The beat is exhilaration laced with grief—she's burning the life she built.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Toll
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. At a river crossing they pay passage from Marta, an old smuggler who once flew with Noor's mother. Marta recognizes the Kestria seal and goes pale, warning them that others have carried this truth and none arrived. The beat is inherited history pressing on the present.

chapters.title: What the Monsoon Takes
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A night storm nearly swamps them; they shelter in a drowned church where the floodwater has lifted coffins into the pews. Cyrus tells Noor why memory is the only justice he trusts. The beat is intimacy forged in shared peril.

chapters.title: Hale Closes the Distance
chapters.summary: Hale's POV, first time. He reports to Crane that the chest has surfaced, and we learn the inspector's cold pragmatism—and his private doubt about the man he serves. The beat is menace with a hairline crack of conscience.

chapters.title: The Witness at Wrenfall
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. They detour to find Sela Ivo, the last living adult from Merrow's Bend, now a deaf herbalist. She confirms the massacre in trembling handwriting and gives them a second document she has hidden for twenty years. The beat is the past given a living voice.

chapters.title: A Favor Called In
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. They reach her old mentor, Judge Ansel Rook, who once promised to help if she ever found something worth the risk. Rook agrees to hear the case but warns the courthouse will be Crane's first target. The beat is hope that feels like a trap.

chapters.title: The Betrayal at the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Rook's clerk, bought by Hale, sells their location; the boathouse is raided. Noor and Cyrus escape through the flooded streets with the documents but lose Sela's testimony to the river. The beat is betrayal and the cost of trusting institutions.

chapters.title: Crane's Offer
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Hale corners them at gunpoint and, instead of killing them, delivers Crane's offer: amnesty, her airstrip back, Cyrus's record expunged—in exchange for the chest. Noor sees Hale's hands aren't steady. The beat is temptation wearing a reasonable face.

chapters.title: Why Cyrus Vane Drowned
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, flashback-heavy. He tells Noor the full truth: he didn't just falsify a record—he let his lover, a Kestrian archivist, take the blame and vanish. Noor's fury and his surrender of all excuses. The beat is love tested by the worst version of the truth.

chapters.title: The Plane in the Flood
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. They attempt to fly the documents to the capital over the storm, and her beloved plane goes down in the flooded lowlands. Both survive; the chest is swept into the current. The beat is devastating loss—everything now depends on the river's mercy.

chapters.title: What the River Gives Back
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Searching the floodline at dawn, they find the chest wedged in a willow, water-stained but legible—barely. Hale finds them, weapon drawn, and Noor appeals to the crack in his conscience, showing him the village's name in his own dead brother's hand. The beat is the climax of persuasion, not force.

chapters.title: The Inspector's Choice
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Hale lets them go and delivers a false report, then walks into Crane's office with the original orders and his resignation. Crane orders him shot; Hale escapes wounded into the flooded city. The beat is a minor character earning his redemption at terrible cost.

chapters.title: The Last Honest Court
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Through rioting streets, they reach Rook's courthouse as Crane's men arrive to burn it. In a chaotic hearing before journalists and fleeing clerks, the documents are read aloud—Merrow's Bend entered into the record. The beat is the climax: justice outside the law forcing its way back inside it.

chapters.title: Crane at the Waterline
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cornered on the courthouse steps as the flood peaks, Crane offers Cyrus his old life back one final time. Cyrus refuses, and Crane—unrepentant to the last—is arrested by his own guards, who have heard the reading. The beat is the fall of the man who signed memory away.

chapters.title: After the Water Falls
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Weeks later: trials beginning, Sela's name restored to a memorial, Hale testifying from a wheelchair. Noor and Cyrus stand at the rebuilt airstrip, neither sure what they are to each other yet, both unwilling to pretend otherwise. The beat is quiet, earned tenderness.

chapters.title: Cyrus and the Compass
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, closing. Cyrus gives her the chest's brass compass—Kestrian-made, its needle pointing not north but toward Merrow's Bend's coordinates. She files a new flight plan, first passenger: Cyrus. The beat is resolution: she flies not to disappear, but to remember out loud.
